note.explanation: Transmission modes describe the direction and timing of data flow between devices. Simplex is one-way, Half-Duplex is two-way but takes turns, and Full-Duplex is two-way at the same time.
note.simple: Ask two questions: Can data go both ways? Can it go both ways at the same time?
note.checkQuestion: Two people use walkie-talkies and take turns speaking. Which transmission mode is this?
note.title: Choosing a Transmission Mode
steps: Check whether data travels in one direction or both directions.
If it travels in one direction only, the mode is Simplex.
If it travels in both directions but the devices take turns, the mode is Half-Duplex.
If both devices can send and receive at the same time, the mode is Full-Duplex.
note.answer: Simplex sends in one direction only; Half-Duplex allows both directions one at a time; Full-Duplex allows both directions simultaneously.

mcqs.stem: A device sends data to another device, and data never travels back. Which transmission mode is being used?
rationales: This is correct because Simplex communication sends data in one direction only.
This is incorrect because Half-Duplex allows data to travel both ways, but not at the same time.
This is incorrect because Full-Duplex allows data to travel both ways simultaneously.
This is incorrect because circuit switching is a method of establishing a communication path, not a transmission mode described here.

options: A keyboard sending data to a computer
Two people talking on a modern telephone
Two users taking turns with walkie-talkies
Two computers sending and receiving data at the same time
mcqs.stem: Which is an example of Simplex communication?
rationales: This is correct because the keyboard sends data to the computer in one direction.
This is incorrect because a modern telephone conversation is an example of Full-Duplex communication.
This is incorrect because taking turns in both directions is Half-Duplex communication.
This is incorrect because simultaneous communication in both directions is Full-Duplex.

options: Data travels in one direction only.
Data travels in both directions, but devices take turns.
Data travels in both directions at the same time.
Data is sent only after being encrypted.
rationales: This is incorrect because one-way data flow describes Simplex communication.
This is correct because Half-Duplex allows both directions, but only one device transmits at a time.
This is incorrect because simultaneous two-way data flow describes Full-Duplex communication.
This is incorrect because encryption does not define a transmission mode.

mcqs.stem: A telephone conversation lets both people talk and listen at the same time. Which mode does this show?
rationales: This is incorrect because Simplex communication is one-way.
This is incorrect because Half-Duplex devices take turns transmitting.
This is correct because Full-Duplex allows both devices to transmit and receive simultaneously.
This is incorrect because Full-Duplex directly describes the situation.

mcqs.stem: A walkie-talkie user must wait for the other person to finish speaking before replying. Which mode is this?
rationales: This is incorrect because Full-Duplex allows simultaneous two-way communication.
This is incorrect because Simplex allows communication in only one direction.
This is correct because Half-Duplex allows both directions, but the users take turns.
This is incorrect because packet switching is a way of sending data in packets, not the mode shown here.

options: The size of the computer screen
mcqs.stem: What feature is used to distinguish Simplex, Half-Duplex, and Full-Duplex communication?
rationales: This is correct because the modes describe the direction and timing of data flow.
This is incorrect because device colour does not determine a communication mode.
This is incorrect because screen size does not determine a communication mode.
This is incorrect because installed programs do not determine a communication mode.

options: A television signal received by viewers
A telephone conversation where both people can speak at once
A keyboard sending keystrokes to a computer
mcqs.stem: Which situation is the best example of Full-Duplex communication?
rationales: This is incorrect because a one-way broadcast to viewers is Simplex communication.
This is correct because both people can send and receive at the same time.
This is incorrect because turn-taking is Half-Duplex communication.
This is incorrect because a keyboard sending data to a computer is Simplex communication.

mcqs.stem: Which mode allows both devices to transmit and receive data simultaneously?
rationales: This is incorrect because Simplex communication sends data in one direction only.
This is incorrect because Half-Duplex devices cannot transmit simultaneously.
This is correct because Full-Duplex permits simultaneous data flow in both directions.
This is incorrect because the situation describes active two-way communication.

steps.why: The textbook gives keyboard-to-computer communication as its Simplex example.
steps.text: Keyboard to computer is an example of simplex communication.

steps.why: Data travels from the keyboard to the computer, in one direction.

example.question: Identify the transmission mode in this example: Keyboard to computer.

explain.title: Simplex: one direction
explain.body: In Simplex communication, data transmission is unidirectional, meaning it flows in only one direction. The keyboard sends data to the computer; data does not travel back along this communication.

explain.title: Half-Duplex: both directions, taking turns
explain.body: In Half-Duplex communication, data transmission can occur in both directions, but not simultaneously. One device must wait for the other to finish transmitting before it can start. Walkie-talkies are a useful example.

explain.title: Full-Duplex: both directions at once
explain.body: Full-duplex communication allows for simultaneous data delivery in both directions. Both devices may transmit and receive data simultaneously at the same time. Telephone conversations are an example.

mistakes: Do not call Half-Duplex one-way communication: it works in both directions, but devices take turns.
Do not say Full-Duplex devices must wait for each other; they can send and receive simultaneously.

Do not confuse the direction of communication with the direction a person is speaking in an example. Identify whether the devices can communicate one way, take turns, or communicate both ways at once.
For the numerical, do not divide kilobytes directly by a rate in bits per second; first convert the size to bits.
